game.name: Doloc Town
game.intro: Doloc Town is a side-scrolling pixel-art farming sim set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. Play as a young scavenger who builds a vertical farm one platform at a time under extreme weather: acid rain, scorching heat and thunderstorms. Gather 40+ resources, fish, ranch, modify crop genes, fight alongside your drone and automate production with solar power. The 1.0 full release on August 6, 2026 adds a complete story ending, the Old City Ruins area, farming automation and 37 new achievements.
keyFacts: 1.0 full release: August 6, 2026 with complete story ending
30+ hours of core gameplay, 100+ hours of additional content
Farming automation: solar power → drone stations (new in 1.0)
Crop gene system: ~20 mutations across 30+ crops
Extreme weather you can turn to your advantage (acid rain, storms, drought)
80 Steam achievements total (43 base + 37 new in 1.0)
aboutPoints: Doloc Town is developed by RedSaw Games Studio and published by Logoi Games with Pathea Games as co-publisher.
The game left Early Access on August 6, 2026 after launching in EA on May 8, 2025.
Information on this site is fact-checked against the official Steam store page, official 1.0 announcement, publisher news and reputable media (CGMagazine, PCGamesN, RPGamer).
Community-sourced details are marked with a ⚠️ note until checked against cited sources.

pages.title: How to Play Doloc Town
pages.metaTitle: How to Play Doloc Town: Complete Beginner's Guide (1.0)
pages.metaDescription: New to Doloc Town? Learn the scavenge-farm-build-explore loop, vertical farms, extreme weather tricks, drone combat and 1.0 automation.
pages.intro: Doloc Town mixes a side-scrolling platformer with a post-apocalyptic farming sim. You start as a scavenger and end as a farming tycoon — here is the full loop, from day one to drones.

sections.heading: The Five-Step Core Loop
sections.body: Every Doloc Town session follows the same rhythm. Once the loop clicks, the wasteland stops being hostile and starts being your farm.
items: Clear the ruins
Break debris and abandoned structures with your starting tools. Clearing opens build space, reveals buried resources and extends your reach. Prioritise plots closest to your home base first.
Gather resources
Collect 40+ minerals, plants, scraps and machine parts. Even junk has a purpose: scrap feeds crafting, plants feed cooking, and minerals upgrade your tech tree. Learn which spots respawn daily.
Farm vertically

Craft planters and stack platforms to build upward. A single horizontal field is a drought risk and a storm magnet; vertical layers give you room to spread crops, protect them and add automation later.
Build and upgrade
Spend resources on the tech tree, blueprints, buildings and your home. Tech Points come from Guildmaster Bellad's quests — always keep one quest active.
Explore new regions
Use upgraded tools and your drone to reach new areas, including the 1.0 Old City Ruins. Exploration feeds back into the loop with new seeds, fish and materials.

sections.heading: Vertical Farming: How It Actually Works
sections.body: The side-scrolling view is not a gimmick — it is the whole farm system.
items: Platforms stack freely; each level you climb adds buildable surface.
Jump and climb between levels — platforming is part of the daily loop, not a loading screen.
Planters sit on platforms; group crops by season so you can re-plant in one pass.
Build covers or use the Rain gene so storms and acid rain do not wipe a whole layer.
Leave vertical gaps for drone flight paths — automation in 1.0 needs clear lanes.

sections.heading: Weather Effects & How to Weaponize Them
sections.body: Extreme weather is the game's signature. It kills careless farms and powers clever ones.
rows: Build covers; collect acid as a crafting resource
Water on a timer; plant heat-resistant gene strains
Harness lightning to charge farm power (key for 1.0 automation)
Let it irrigate for free; save watering energy
Protect crops and plan watering before Month 4

sections.heading: First Week: The 5 Moves That Set Up the Run
sections.body: Do these in order and the first season stops being a scramble.
items: Clear your starting plot fully
Hidden corners hide scrap that funds your first planter batch.
Plant fast crops first
Quick harvests generate the capital for tools and seeds.
Talk to every villager daily
Friendship unlocks recipes, tech and story; it also triggers Blooming Friendship.
Open Bellad's quests immediately
Quest rewards are Tech Points — the only reliable early tech income.
Start stockpiling before Month 4
Prepare crop protection and watering before Month 4.

sections.heading: Day One: What to Do First
sections.body: The first in-game day sets your momentum more than any other. This priority list is community-verified for 1.0 — exact shop prices are player-reported. [L2]
items: Unlock the backpack upgrade first
Community reports: find the tech merchant and buy the first backpack tier — it roughly doubles your slots and stops the constant trips home.
Do a villager quest on day one
Quests pay cash and Tech Points — the best minute-for-minute investment in the whole opening.
Plant Endyams early
A slow-maturing staple that pays off all season — community consensus is to get it in the ground on day one.
Clear your starting plot fully
Hidden corners hide scrap that funds your first planter batch.
Pick up the free fishing rod
The Lightman fishing tutorial hands you a rod — free gear, no reason to skip it.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes New Players Make (Avoid These)
sections.body: The most common early run-enders, from community reports: watering everything by hand every single day (automate or use the Rain gene), planting one giant flat field (a single storm wipes it), ignoring friendship (you lock yourself out of recipes), skipping Bellad's quests (you fall behind the tech tree), and failing to protect crops before Month 4 (Harsh Dry Season can ruin an unprepared field).

sections.heading: Drone Combat: Controls, Then Strategy
sections.body: Your drone is both weapon and survival tool. Learn the controls, then the builds.
items: RMB locks on, LMB fires, Space dodges, R reloads.
Upgrade chassis (survivability), barrel (damage) and battery (uptime) — in that order early on.
Charge beam (F) breaks shields on armoured Scavenger Bugs; normal fire bounces off.
Fit weapon and lighting modules before exploring ruins at night.
Rare fish drop advanced parts — fishing funds your combat build.

sections.heading: What the 1.0 Release Changes for New Players
sections.body: The August 6, 2026 1.0 release reshapes the early game.
items: 1.0 launches: complete story ending, Old City Ruins, farming automation, Mushroom Fest, 37 new achievements.
New players
You can reach the official two-stage farming automation earlier than EA players.
Old City Ruins
New region with fierce enemies, new NPCs, side quests and resources; many paths lead there.
⚠️ Verification
Exact unlock order and build costs are still being verified in 1.0; details marked with ⚠️ are community-sourced.

sections.heading: Quick Answers for New Players
items: Is Doloc Town single-player?
Yes. The developers confirmed the 1.0 release is a single-player experience; co-op/multiplayer may be discussed later based on community feedback.
Do I have to water every day?
Yes at the start — but the Rain gene auto-waters neighbours, and 1.0 drone stations automate watering entirely.
Can I build anywhere?
You stack platforms within your farm area. The Old City Ruins (1.0) adds new buildable zones and resources.
How long is Doloc Town?
30+ hours for the core story, 100+ hours with fishing, ranching, genes and collections.
Should I buy it on sale?
It is ¥58 normally with a 20% launch discount (¥46.40) until August 19, 2026 — a good entry point.

pages.title: Doloc Town Farming Automation Guide (1.0)
pages.metaTitle: Doloc Town Farming Automation & Drone Guide (1.0)
pages.metaDescription: How Doloc Town 1.0 farming automation works: two-stage crop automation, task assignment and current drone issues from official notes.
pages.intro: The 1.0 release turns you from a farmer into a farm manager. Here is how to generate clean energy, deploy drone stations and automate the whole crop cycle.

sections.heading: How Farming Automation Works
sections.body: Automation has three layers: energy, stations and drones. Each layer feeds the next, so build in this order.
items: Build the automation chain
Follow the official two-stage farming automation flow and unlock each task before expanding the layout.
Build farming drone stations
Stations are the control points that let drones run farm operations. They consume energy, so size them to your power output.
Assign automated tasks
Drones handle seeding, nurturing plants and gathering yields end-to-end. Start with one repetitive chore (watering) and expand.
Free up your time
While drones work, explore, talk to townsfolk or push the story — this is the point of the whole system.

sections.heading: What to Automate First
sections.body: Start with a small, repeatable crop task and verify that the drone completes it reliably.
items: Start with a low-risk crop task rather than your only income crop.
Leave clear routes around platforms so drones can reach assigned plots.
Save before restructuring a working automated farm.
Official patch 1.00.03 lists drone failures in certain situations as unresolved.

sections.heading: The Industrial Zone & Conveyor Belts
sections.body: Automation is not only for crops.
items: Start the generator in the industrial area
This powers the new conveyor-belt production line added in 1.0.
Build conveyor belts
Move materials automatically between stations and storage.
Unlock previously unreachable areas
The industrial line grants access to new parts of the map and new resources.

sections.heading: Automation Roadmap (Community Draft)
sections.body: A rough order that most players report working — verify exact costs in your save.

sections.heading: Common Automation Mistakes
sections.body: Do not rush stations before you have stable power — a station that idles half the day wastes the whole point. Do not automate your only income crop first; automate a low-value filler crop to learn the system risk-free. And leave clear lanes for drones when you build platforms, or they cannot reach their plots.

sections.heading: Why This Page Matters
sections.body: This page separates official 1.0 and 1.00.03 information from community-reported details. Check the linked Steam announcements after each patch.

pages.metaDescription: How the Doloc Town crop gene system works: gene modules, ~20 mutations like Spore Burst and Rain, seed mother plants, and how to breed stronger crops.
pages.intro: Reclaim pre-apocalypse tech and rewrite the genetics of 30+ crops. Gene modules stack up to three per seed and unlock mutations that change how your farm behaves.

sections.heading: How the Gene System Works
sections.body: Reclaim pre-apocalypse tech and rewrite the genetics of 30+ crops. Every seed carries up to three gene modules; the right combo turns a plain crop into a self-watering, self-replicating machine.
items: Use gene readers, replicators and synthesizers to inspect and breed seeds.
Unlock seed mother plants via the shop, Aurora seed research and wild mothers.
Stack up to 3 modules per seed — synergy matters more than raw numbers.
Gene lab locations and module sources are still being verified in 1.0 (⚠️).

sections.heading: Known Gene Mutations (Community-Verified)
sections.body: These mutations are widely reported by the community; the full 1.0 list is being compiled.
rows: Dry-season insurance; pairs with Spore Burst

sections.heading: How to Breed Stronger Seeds
sections.body: Follow the mother-plant pipeline.
items: Get a seed mother plant
Buy from the shop, complete Aurora seed research, or find wild mothers.
Extract its genes
Use the gene reader to pull modules.
Combine up to 3 modules
Synthesize a custom seed.
Plant and observe
Watch the synergy on your farm; record which combos thrive in which season.

sections.heading: Pro Tips & Common Mistakes
sections.body: Pair Rain with auto-harvest mutations for a nearly hands-free plot — the community's favourite combo. Gift of Time rewards long runs, so plant it early. Common mistakes: over-stacking redundant modules instead of building synergy, and ignoring the mother-plant research track (it gates the best modules). ⚠️ Community-sourced; verify in your own save.

sections.heading: How to Fish Efficiently
sections.body: Turn fishing from a side activity into a reliable income and parts source.
items: Map the ponds: each body of water has its own fish pool — check the tables above before choosing a spot
Upgrade your rod: higher-tier rods unlock better fish and make the fishing minigame more forgiving
Fish through weather: rain and thunderstorms bring uncommon catches that dry days don't
Watch the season: rainy season (Jan–Feb) and dry season (Mar–Apr) change the catch tables completely
Breed rare fish: the 13 tank-only species need specific parents — keep spares instead of selling everything
Rare fish drop advanced drone and tool parts, so a good fishing session funds your upgrades

sections.heading: Fishing Tips: Common Failures & Fixes
sections.body: A lot of early fishing frustration comes down to rod level and timing, not luck. These tips come from community experience — treat the numbers as player-reported until we verify them in 1.0. [L2]
items: Do the Lightman fishing tutorial first — it gives you a free rod, so you are not stuck with the starting stick.
Upgrade your rod early: community reports say a Level 2 rod (~1,000 coins) can catch every fish in the game, and higher-tier rods make the minigame noticeably more forgiving.
Controller players report the most failures: if a catch keeps slipping on a gamepad, upgrade the rod before assuming your timing is the problem.
Fish through weather: rain and thunderstorms bring catches that dry days never do — check the tables above before choosing a spot.
Dry your catch instead of selling raw: fish + dryer is the easiest early money loop (see our money-making guide).
Keep one of each species: rare fish drop advanced drone and tool parts, and 13 tank-only species need specific parents to breed.

pages.title: Doloc Town Drone Combat Guide: Upgrades & Modules
pages.metaTitle: Doloc Town Drone Combat: Builds, Upgrades & Best Modules
pages.metaDescription: Master Doloc Town drone combat: chassis, barrel and battery upgrades, tactical mods, and how to beat armored enemies.
pages.intro: Your drone is a buildable combat platform. Upgrade its chassis, barrel and battery, fit tactical modules and learn to break armored enemies — here is the full combat picture.

sections.heading: Drone Combat Controls
sections.body: Four inputs cover everything in a fight — learn them before worrying about builds.
items: RMB: lock on target
LMB: fire
Space: dodge / dash
R: reload
F: charge beam (breaks shields)

sections.heading: Core Upgrades & What Each Changes
sections.body: Every upgrade changes how fights play, not just numbers.

sections.heading: Notable Modules (Community-Sourced)
sections.body: Modules define your combat identity.

sections.heading: Build Order for Combat
sections.body: A reliable early progression.
items: Upgrade battery first
Running out of energy mid-fight is the #1 new-player death.
Then barrel
More damage per energy spent.
Fit a tactical module
Capacitor/Shadow Shooter scale with your build.
Save parts from fishing
Rare fish drop advanced parts — fish to fund combat.

sections.heading: Combat Tactics by Situation
sections.body: Adapt to the enemy, not the other way around.
items: Armored Scavenger Bugs ignore normal fire — charge the beam (F) to break their shield, then unload.
Always reload behind cover; reloading in the open gets you hit.
Dodge toward open space, not into walls — panic-dodging into geometry is a classic death.
Equip a lighting module before night ruin runs, and don't fight at night without it.
The Wetlands boss drops a Medium E-chip — farm it for higher-tier builds ⚠️.

sections.heading: Fighting Scavenger Bugs (And Avoiding Mistakes)
sections.body: Armoured Scavenger Bugs ignore normal fire. Charge the beam (F) to break their shield, then unload. Common mistakes: panic-dodging into walls, reloading in the open, and fighting at night without a lighting module. ⚠️ Details from community guides; verify in 1.0.

sections.heading: Quick Answers
items: How do I break armored enemies?
Use the charge beam (F) to break shields — normal fire bounces off armored Scavenger Bugs.
What should I upgrade first?
Battery. Running out of energy mid-fight is the #1 new-player death; then barrel for damage.
Where do advanced parts drop?
Rare fish drop advanced drone and tool parts; the Wetlands boss drops a Medium E-chip ⚠️.
Is night combat viable?
Yes, but only with a lighting module fitted — otherwise enemies see you before you see them.
What are the best modules?
Tactical Capacitor (bonus damage after reload) and Shadow Shooter (chance to fire twice) are the community favorites ⚠️.

sections.heading: The Three Mysteries (And Common Mistakes)
sections.body: Why does the River Valley stay lush in a ruined world? What happened to the town's vanished leader? Why do so many pre-apocalypse tech pieces carry the mark of 'Eden'? Common mistake: rushing past lore objects — several story beats are missable if you sprint the region.

sections.heading: Quick Answers
items: How many regions are there?
Five base regions (Outskirts, River Valley, Wetlands, Caves and the Old City Ruins added in 1.0). The Old City Ruins is described as the game's third major area.
What is new in the 1.0 Old City Ruins?
A major new region with fierce enemies, new NPCs and companions, side quests and endgame crafting resources.
Where can I find Kumasang?
Kumasang is a roaming NPC in the River Valley and a source of rare materials ⚠️.
Can I explore ruins at night?
Yes, but fit a lighting module to your drone first — night fights without light are the classic mistake.
How do I get advanced drone parts?
Rare fish drop advanced drone and tool parts; the Wetlands boss drops a Medium E-chip ⚠️.

pages.intro: Farming is the foundation of your wasteland farm. Learn what to plant, when, how to protect it from extreme weather — and how genes and 1.0 automation replace the busywork.

sections.heading: Crop Basics
sections.body: Farming in Doloc Town is vertical: you stack planters on platforms and climb between them every day. Get the basics right and the rest of the game funds itself.
items: Seasonal crops rotate with the calendar — plant to the season and replant after each changeover.
Fruit trees take 7 days and produce forever once mature — plant them in week one.
Herbs grow in 2 days — fast filler crops that smooth cash flow between harvests.
Mushrooms are an autumn forage bonus — free calories that cost no water.
A sickle harvests whole groups at once — upgrade it early, it is the biggest time-saver in the game.
Crops can be gene-modified: the 1.0 store page confirms the genetics system covers upward of 30 different crops.

sections.heading: The Farm Calendar: Seasons & Weather
sections.body: Doloc Town runs a two-season weather year on top of a four-month calendar. The rainy season (January–February) and dry season (March–April) change what you can grow and catch — and April is the drought month.

High-value crops where extra fruit = extra income

sections.heading: Protecting Crops from Weather
sections.body: Weather protection is a strategy, not an afterthought.
items: Watch the forecast daily
Acid rain, heat and storms all threaten fields — know what is coming.
Build covers

Use the Rain gene

sections.heading: From Hand-Farming to Automation (1.0)
sections.body: The 1.0 release turns you from a farmer into a farm manager. The upgrade path is: energy first, stations second, then let the drones work.
items: Follow the two-stage automation tasks described in the official 1.0 notes.
Construct farm drone stations — the control points that let drones work the fields.
Assign automation tasks: drones handle seeding, nurturing and harvesting end to end.
Vertical stacking matters: leave clear flight lanes between platforms so drones can reach every planter.
The industrial zone adds conveyor-belt production lines that open up previously unreachable areas.

sections.heading: Drought Strategy & Common Mistakes
sections.body: Month 4 is Harsh Dry Season. Protect exposed crops, plan watering and keep a save before changing automation. The cited official notes do not establish a price-arbitrage strategy.

sections.heading: Quick Answers
items: Do I have to water every day?
Early on, yes — but the Rain Falls Evenly gene auto-waters surrounding crops, and 1.0 drone stations fully take over.
When should I plant fruit trees?
Week one. They take 7 days to mature and then produce forever — the earlier they go in, the more free income you bank.
What is the drought month?
Month 4 is Harsh Dry Season. Prepare crop protection and watering.
How do gene modules work?
Each seed holds up to 3 gene modules chosen from a pool of around 20 mutations; install them with the gene reader/synthesizer and observe the synergy on your farm.
How many crops can be gene-modified?
The official store page says the genetics system covers upward of 30 different crops.
Does 1.0 fully automate farming?
Yes. Official 1.0 notes describe two-stage farming automation; patch 1.00.03 also lists drone failures in certain situations.

Old City Ruins, complete story ending, farming automation, Mushroom Fest, new tools/drones/fish/accessories and 37 new achievements.

GamersGate lists it as an authorized retailer at 20% off (US$19.99 → US$15.99), but it showed "Out of stock" in both its US and Singapore storefronts when we checked on August 8, 2026 — so Steam is the reliable route right now. GamersGate keys are also region-locked to the country you buy from.
Is there a Supporter Pack?
Yes — a 3-item bundle: the game plus the Digital Artbook and the Original Soundtrack, US$22.92 down to US$19.32 (16% off) on Steam. It is optional and not needed to play the full game.
Is Doloc Town multiplayer?
No — the developers confirmed 1.0 is a single-player experience. Co-op is not ruled out for the future.
What languages are supported?
9 languages at 1.0: English, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian.
Will my Early Access save carry over?
The 1.0 release continues the same game — Early Access saves carry into the full version (verify on the Steam page before updating).

pages.title: How Long Does Doloc Town Take to Beat?
pages.metaTitle: How Long Is Doloc Town? 30–100+ Hours to Beat (2026)
pages.metaDescription: How long is Doloc Town? 30+ hours main story, 40–60 relaxed, 100+ for 100% completion — from the official store numbers.
pages.intro: Doloc Town is a deep farming sim, so play time depends on how much you want to do. The official store page gives clear numbers.

sections.heading: Official Play Time
sections.body: From the official Steam store page and the 1.0 announcement.
rows: Story, main quests and core farm progression
All 80 achievements, full gene research, fishing, ranching, automation
Core story plus a comfortable amount of side content
Story and main systems, skipping optional collecting

sections.heading: What Makes It Long
sections.body: The systems that add the most play time.
items: 80 Steam achievements (43 base + 37 new in 1.0) encourage full completion
Crop gene system: ~20 mutations across 30+ crops to research and breed
Fishing: different ponds, rods and weather give different catches — completing the catalog takes a while
Two-stage farming automation is a progression system to build toward
The 5 regions plus the new Old City Ruins area add exploration time

sections.heading: How to Play Faster (or Longer)
sections.body: Set the pace you want.
items: To finish the story quickly: focus on main quests and town tasks, and let automation handle routine farming
To 100%: work on achievements, the gene lab and the fish catalog in parallel — don't save them for the end
Season weather matters: use storms to water and thunderstorms to store power instead of fighting them
Prepare crop protection and watering before Month 4's Harsh Dry Season

sections.heading: Length FAQ
items: How long is Doloc Town?
The official store page lists 30+ hours of core gameplay and 100+ hours of additional content for full completion.
Is 100% completion realistic?
Yes, but it's a marathon — 100+ hours across all 80 achievements, gene research, fishing and automation.
Does the gene system add much time?
Yes — researching ~20 mutations across 30+ crops is one of the longest optional systems.
Is there post-game content?
The Old City Ruins area and achievement hunting extend play after the main story ends.
Is Doloc Town worth it for the time investment?
At ¥46.40 during launch, the cost-per-hour is very low for a 30+ hour game — good value if you like farming sims.

pages.title: How to Make Money Fast in Doloc Town
pages.metaTitle: Doloc Town Money Guide: Fast Income (1.0)
pages.metaDescription: Fast ways to make money in Doloc Town: process crops and fish for +10-20%, dry your catch, sell into the drought spike and the Day-1 moves that set up income.
pages.intro: Money in Doloc Town is rarely about selling raw crops. Processing, weather timing and one early upgrade change the math completely — here is what the community has figured out.

sections.heading: The Money Loop, From Zero
sections.body: Income in Doloc Town compounds: each layer multiplies what the last one earned. Build them in this order.
items: Buy the backpack upgrade on day one — community reports say the first tier from the tech merchant roughly doubles your slots, which stops the hours lost walking home.
Run villager quests — they pay cash and Tech Points, the two things early money-making scales with.
Plant Endyams early — a slow staple that keeps paying all season; get it in the ground on day one.
Fish through weather and dry the catch — the easiest loop in the game (detailed below).
Process crops instead of selling raw — pickling, drying and weaving each add 10-20% value.

sections.heading: Processing: The 10-20% Value Add
sections.body: Community reports (L2) put the margin from processing at 10-20% per item. The machines run around the clock, so the margin compounds while you do anything else. Exact 1.0 margins are pending our own testing.

sections.heading: The Easiest Starter Loop: Fish, Dry, Sell
sections.body: This is the community's most-recommended early routine: low risk, no seed cost, and it funds everything else.
items: Get the free rod
Do the Lightman fishing tutorial — it gives you a rod so you start the loop with zero cost.
Fish through weather
Rain and thunderstorms bring catches dry days never do — check the fishing guide's tables first.
Dry instead of selling raw
A dryer adds 10-20% value [L2]; the loop becomes fish → dry → sell.
Upgrade the rod when you can
A Level 2 rod (~1,000 coins) can catch every fish per community reports [L2].
Keep breeding pairs
13 tank-only species need specific parents — keep spares, sell the surplus.

sections.heading: Season Planning
sections.body: Use the official calendar to schedule crops and fishing without assuming an unverified price mechanic.
items: Month 4 is Harsh Dry Season — protect crops and plan watering.
Rainy season (Jan-Feb) reshuffles the fish tables — fish the uncommon catches while they last.
Thunderstorms charge your farm's power — in 1.0 that cuts the running costs of automation.
Plant for the season — off-season crops wither, so rotate what you grow with the calendar.

sections.heading: Common Money Mistakes
sections.body: Community reports flag these as the ways players leave money on the table: selling everything raw (you skip the 10-20% processing margin), not stockpiling before Month 4 (you sell at the worst prices of the year), skipping quests (you miss Tech Points, the income multiplier), selling every fish (you lose the breeding pairs for 13 tank-only species), and delaying the backpack upgrade (hours lost running home).

sections.heading: Sources & Verification
sections.body: The 10-20% processing margins, the Level 2 rod and the Day-1 backpack tips are community-reported (L2, e.g. grindnstrat and Steam discussions). We have not verified exact margins in the 1.0 client yet — treat specific numbers as player-reported and confirm in your own save.

sections.heading: Quick Answers
items: What is the fastest way to make money in Doloc Town?
The community consensus is fish → dry → sell: no seed cost, works from day one, and the dryer adds 10-20% value [L2].
How much value does processing add?
Pickling, drying and weaving each add roughly 10-20% per item, per community reports [L2].
When should I sell my stockpile?
The cited official notes do not establish a Month 4 trading strategy; plan crop protection and watering instead.
Is the backpack upgrade worth it?
Yes — the first tier roughly doubles your slots and is the community's most-recommended first purchase [L2].
Do I need money for automation?
Later, yes: the automation progression costs materials and Tech Points, so early income supports the 1.0 endgame.
